column1: # Pronunciation table for say.py.
# Format: one entry per line, the word, a TAB, then the respelling.
#   word<TAB>respelling
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. A line without exactly one
# TAB is skipped with a warning on stderr.
# Matching:
# - Case-insensitive, whole words only: "project" matches "Project" and
#   "project's", not "projector". A word may be several words ("git log");
#   any run of spaces in the text matches.
# - Longer entries are tried first. Replacement is one pass, so a respelling
#   is never matched again.
# - The respelling is used as written. Its first letter is capitalised when
#   the matched word starts with a capital. Capitals inside a respelling
#   ("PRAH-ject") mark stress for the reader; the voice does not spell them out.
# - There are no context rules: every match is replaced. For a word whose
#   reading depends on context, give a per-request hint instead:
#   say.py --say-as project=pruh-JECT "..."
# Order: this file, then each pronounce-*.tsv beside it, sorted by name (your
# own tables; git ignores them, so they survive updates to this file), then
# each table in SHIPS_COMPUTER_PRONOUNCE (colon-separated paths), then each
# --say-as hint. A later entry for the same word wins.
project
